extracted.intended_audience: inventors, patent agents, and colonial officials handling patent applications in British colonies (late 19th century)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and substantive standards governing the filing, examination, grant, maintenance, amendment, opposition, infringement, and registration of patents (and exclusive privileges) in various British colonies; includes procedural time limits, fees, provisional protection, and remedies. Geared to applicants and officials applying British-model patent law in colonial jurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application contents (petition, declaration, specification, drawings, claims)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents/applications must be accompanied by a petition, declaration, and specification; the specification should contain a declaration of authorship, a description of the invention illustrated with necessary drawings, and claims of the inventions or combinations claimed as new.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifications and drawings are often required in duplicate; the specification must be limited to one invention in some colonies; signatures, attestation by witnesses, and place and date of signature may be required; where the applicant acts by agent a power of attorney may be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of attorney requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications for patents must be accompanied by a power of attorney, bearing the English stamp duty; proved as required by the local statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Power of attorney allows an agent to sign documents on behalf of the applicant; must comply with local proof formalities (e.g., 27 Vict. chap. 17 referenced).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees and stamp duties (application, sealing, annuities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Various government fees and stamp duties are payable: e.g. the letters patent bear a stamp duty of £1 10s; fees for reference to the Attorney-General (e.g. £5); duties payable at termination of three and seven years; fees on application, sealing, disclaimer, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee schedules vary by colony and include payments on lodging applications, filing complete specifications, obtaining letters patent, and periodic duties (renewal/annuity fees) typically at years 3 and 7 or in installments; failure to pay may void the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent term and possible extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents are generally granted for fourteen years; in many colonies extensions are authorised for further terms not exceeding seven (or in exceptional cases fourteen) years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions are subject to statutory procedures and may require petitions and/or Court or Governor-in-Council reports (e.g., report that the patentee has not been adequately remunerated). Fees are payable on petitions for extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent void if earlier patent exists elsewhere
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent becomes void with the expiration or determination of any earlier patent elsewhere for the same invention; no patent granted in the colony after the determination of an earlier patent elsewhere is valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents overlapping rights; provisions to extend foreign/UK patents into the colony are separate and limited by the original term of the foreign patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional protection / certificate system
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may deposit a provisional specification and obtain provisional protection (e.g., six or twelve months) or a certificate from the relevant official; after provisional deposit a complete specification must be left within the statutory period (commonly nine months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional certificates often protect the invention for a short period to allow filing of a full specification; complete specification must be lodged within prescribed time (e.g., nine months) and accepted within 12 months or the application may become void; deposit of provisional protection may date patents as of the provisional deposit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registrar/examiner examination duties
rubrics_metrics.description: The Registrar (or examiners under direction) must examine each application to ascertain whether the nature of the invention is described, that papers are prepared as prescribed, and that the title sufficiently describes the subject-matter; the Registrar may refuse the application or require amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners report to the Registrar who may refuse or require amendments; refusal of acceptance is generally subject to appeal to the Court; the Registrar hears opposed cases with witnesses and may adjourn hearings and require deposits for costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertisement and opposition periods
rubrics_metrics.description: An acceptance of a specification is advertised in the Gazette and oppositions can be entered within a statutory period (commonly two months, in some colonies one month) from the advertisement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oppositions are heard by the Registrar (or other authority); decisions are subject to appeal to the Court; specific opposition timeframes vary by colony (e.g., Mauritius and Newfoundland one month; New Zealand two months).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of infringement proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: No proceedings for infringement can be taken until after the grant/sealing of the patent; generally no action for infringements committed before the publication or sealing of the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent rights often relate back to the date of acceptance or sealing for territorial effect, but legal remedies for infringement are only enforceable after formal grant/publication as prescribed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments of specifications (limits and procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments of the specification may be made by leave of the Registrar (subject to appeal to the Court); no amendment is to be allowed that will make the specification, as amended, claim an invention substantially larger than, or substantially different from, the invention originally claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leave to amend is conclusive except in case of fraud; amendments may be applied for and opposed by any person; amendments may also be permitted by Court/judge during actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedy where patentee has overclaimed by mistake
rubrics_metrics.description: If it is proved that by mistake, accident, or inadvertence the patentee claimed something of which he was not the inventor, the patent shall be deemed valid for so much of the invention as shall actually be his own; a Commissioner may, if satisfied the error arose from inadvertence and not fraud, and upon surrender and filing of an amended specification, grant a new patent for the unexpired term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treble damages remain recoverable for unlawful users of the patentee's patented invention that legitimately falls within his true claim; fees (e.g., £10) may be payable on such regrants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclaimers and memoranda of alteration
rubrics_metrics.description: Patentees are at liberty, with leave of the appropriate officer, to enter disclaimers or memoranda of alteration; fees are payable on each such application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclaimers and memoranda allow the patentee to correct/surrender parts of the claim or specification; fees vary by colony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration of assignments and licences
rubrics_metrics.description: All assignments and licences must be registered in the Register of Proprietors; assignments executed in the United Kingdom or elsewhere (not within the colonies) must be registered within a statutory period (e.g., ninety days).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to register may affect record title; registration fees are payable (e.g., 1s or £1 depending on colony).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public inspection of registers and correction power
rubrics_metrics.description: Registers under the Act are open to public inspection and extracts may be obtained; entries in the registers may be corrected by the Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registers contain names/addresses of grantees, notifications of assignments, licences, extensions, amendments, and revocations; public access supports notice and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory licences / working obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Governor (or Minister) is empowered to order the patentee to grant licences on such terms as he may think right where it is proved that by default of the patentee to grant licences on reasonable terms the patent is not being worked in the colony or the reasonable requirements of the public are not supplied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compulsory licensing powers are a remedy against non-working or refusal to supply the public; applicable procedures, timings, and terms are set by statute and discretionary authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation procedures (petition, scire facias)
rubrics_metrics.description: Revocations of patents may be obtained on petition to the Court; proceedings for revocation are substantially similar to those in the British Act, and patents may also be revoked by writ of scire facias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grounds for revocation include lack of novelty, not being first inventor, insufficient specification, or non-working (in some colonies); judicial process and appeals to higher courts (including Privy Council) may apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working requirement enforcement (assignment or use for consideration)
rubrics_metrics.description: An inventor may be required to assign his right, or to grant the use thereof for a consideration to be determined by the Civil Court if the invention has not been put into action within twelve months subsequent to the concession, or if its working shall have been suspended for twelve months continuously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a statutory means to ensure inventions are worked locally; the Court determines compensation/consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Models and physical exhibits
rubrics_metrics.description: The Registrar may require the patentee to furnish a model, on payment to the patentee of the costs of its manufacture; models may be required on deposit in some colonies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Models assist examination and public record; the official may pay for manufacture costs; requirements and timing vary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibition of inventions does not prejudice patents (subject to procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: The exhibition of any invention at industrial, intercolonial, or international exhibitions will not prejudice the patent right provided the prescribed proceedings are taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are statutory protections to allow showcasing inventions internationally without losing novelty, but applicants must follow prescribed procedural steps to preserve rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign vessels/navigation exception
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent will not prevent the use of an invention for the navigation of a foreign vessel within the colonial jurisdiction; similar exceptions apply for foreign ships resorting to the colony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a territorial limitation recognizing sovereign maritime privileges; exceptions may not apply where the foreign state has patent laws that prevent such use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secrecy for war or munitions inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Governor has power to deal with applications for patents for improvements in instruments or munitions of war so that the same may be kept secret, pending a reference to Her Majesty's Principal Secretary of State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This allows secrecy orders for national security; the patent may be withheld from public record while referenced to central authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: International priority (application within prescribed months)
rubrics_metrics.description: By Order in Council the provisions of sect. 108 of the British Patents Act, 1888 may be applied so that a person who has applied for protection in England or a foreign state party to the convention shall have priority in the colony if the colonial application is made within twelve (or in some cases seven) months from the English/foreign application; such colonial patents shall take effect from the same date as the foreign application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Colonies vary in the permitted priority interval (12 months in New Zealand example, 7 months in others); the applicant must timely file colonial application to claim priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees schedule and annuities detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory lists of fees are specified for lodging applications (provisional or complete), filing complete specifications, obtaining letters patent, application to amend, sealing, and payments before the expiration of given years (e.g., 3rd, 7th years), or alternate staged yearly payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must follow local fee schedules; options may exist (one lump sum or staged payments) and there are alternative annuity tables for later years in some colonies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility to apply (who may be applicant)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may apply for a patent: the actual inventor, his assigns, legal representatives of deceased inventors, or persons to whom the invention has been communicated by the inventor (in some cases). Mere importers are not deemed inventors in certain colonies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some colonies allow application by non-residents and by persons holding partial interests; representatives of deceased inventors often have limited time windows (e.g., six months) to apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-invention limitation and claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification must be limited to one invention; every patent is to be granted for one invention only, but may contain more than one claim; no objection can be taken on the ground that it covers more than one invention in some jurisdictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural rules may require limitation to a single invention for the formal application even if multiple claims are drafted to define scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional-to-complete specification consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a provisional specification has been first deposited, the complete specification must be lodged within nine months and the Registrar compares the complete with the provisional to ascertain that the invention is substantially the same; refusal to accept is subject to appeal; the application is void if the specification is not accepted within twelve months from date of application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures applicants do not materially broaden the invention between provisional and complete filings; extensions may be available on payment of fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance dated as of deposit for provisional protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters patent are dated and sealed as of the day of the deposit of the application for provisional protection, but no action can be taken in respect of any infringement committed before the deposit of the complete specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The dating gives priority effect but enforcement awaits completion/publication; applicants should be aware of the difference between priority date and enforceability date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties for false representations and misuse
rubrics_metrics.description: Penalties are imposed on persons falsely representing articles to be patented, for unauthorised assumption of the royal arms, and for making false entries in registers; fines and misdemeanour penalties are prescribed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory penalties deter false patent claims, counterfeit stamps/marks, and fraud in registry documents; amounts and criminal vs fine penalties vary by colony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caveat filing for notice of subsequent applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A caveat may be filed entitling the filer to notice of any application being made for a patent for a similar invention within twelve months from the date of filing; a fee is payable on each caveat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caveats preserve an interested party's right to be notified of later applications and to oppose them; fees and exact protective period vary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importer is not inventor (Mauritius example)
rubrics_metrics.description: The importer into Mauritius of a new invention is not deemed an inventor unless he is the actual inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local rules may expressly exclude mere importers from entitlement to exclusive privileges; actual inventive contribution is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration and conduct of patent agents
rubrics_metrics.description: No person is entitled to call himself a patent agent unless registered as a patent agent under the Act, under penalty (specified sum).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent agents must register and comply with statutory qualifications and the Patent Office rules; unauthorized practice is penalised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deceased inventor representative time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Representatives of deceased inventors may obtain patents provided such applications are made within a statutory period (e.g., six months from the decease).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely filing by legal representatives preserves rights; beyond the period the entitlement may lapse.
